aggregation_effect.explanation: Difference attributable purely to replacing the plain maximum sub-index with a dominant term plus a co-exposure surcharge. The reference cohort carries no vulnerability weighting at all.

per_cohort.rationale: Reference cohort. All vulnerability factors are 1, so the dominant term equals the official CPCB AQI rescaled to 0-100.
Airways are still developing and minute ventilation per kilogram of body mass is higher than in adults, so nitrogen dioxide and ozone carry the largest emphasis.
Reduced cardiopulmonary reserve places the largest documented PM2.5 mortality gradient in this group, with ozone a close second.
Sulfur dioxide and ozone provoke bronchoconstriction within minutes in people with reactive airways, so both are weighted above particulates.
Fine particulate matter triggers ischaemic events and carbon monoxide reduces oxygen delivery, so PM2.5 and CO dominate this profile.
Fine particulate matter is associated with reduced birthweight and preterm birth, and carbon monoxide competes with fetal oxygen transport.
Long outdoor hours and physical exertion raise the inhaled dose; ozone and coarse particulates therefore carry the largest emphasis.

any_cohort_differs.explanation: Share of city-days on which at least one cohort would receive a different advisory band from the one the official AQI implies. This is the headline evidence that a single population-average index under-serves vulnerable groups.

pollutants_excluded_and_why.NH3: Part of the CPCB AQI but cohort-specific health evidence at Indian ambient concentrations is too thin to support a defensible vulnerability factor.
pollutants_excluded_and_why.Benzene/Toluene/Xylene: Sparse coverage in city_day.csv and no cohort-resolved short-term exposure-response basis.

aqi_recomputation_audit.diagnosis: The discrepancy is systematically positive: the supplied AQI exceeds the reconstruction. The bias is largest on days dominated by CO and O3, which are exactly the two species for which the CPCB specification uses the maximum 8-hour running mean rather than the 24-hour mean. Reconstructing from daily means therefore understates those two sub-indices, and no reconstruction from city_day.csv alone can recover them.
aqi_recomputation_audit.decision: The supplied AQI column is used as the supervised target throughout, because it embodies the correct CPCB averaging convention. The recomputed series is used only for auditing and for the HAI sub-index decomposition, where the same approximation applies identically to every cohort and therefore cannot distort the cohort-to-cohort comparison that constitutes the novelty claim.
